chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said:

I said to Zurara: 'Indeed, people narrated to me from him, meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and from his father (peace be upon him), regarding matters of inheritance (al-fara'id). So I will present them to you. Whatever of it is false, say
And I said to him: 'A man narrated to me from one of the two (peace be upon them) regarding two parents and brothers of the mother, that they are barred (blocked) and do not inherit.'
He said: 'This, by Allah, is false. But I will inform you, and I will not narrate to you anything (as a formal hadith). And that which I am saying to you, by Allah, is the truth.'
Indeed, if a man leaves behind his two parents, then for the mother is one-third and for the father is two-thirds in the Book of Allah, Exalted and Majestic.
So if there are brothers for him (meaning for the deceased), meaning brothers of the father and mother, or brothers of the father, then for his mother is one-sixth, and for the father is five-sixths.
And the father is given the extra share due to his dependents.
And as for the brothers of the mother who are not of the father, then they do not block the mother from the one-third, nor do they inherit.

And if a man dies and leaves his mother, and brothers and sisters of the mother and father, and brothers and sisters of the father, and brothers and sisters of the mother, and the father is not alive, then they do not inherit, nor do they block her, because he is not a Kalala (one who has neither parents nor offspring).

key_terms.كَلَالَةً: Kalala (a person with no direct ascendants or descendants)

ai.seo_question: How do different types of siblings affect the mother's inheritance share according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Zurara elucidates the specific mechanics of the 'Hajb' (blocking) in inheritance, distinguishing how paternal siblings reduce the mother's share to one-sixth while maternal siblings do not block her from the one-third share, a nuance derived from the interplay of Quranic verses. The narration further clarifies the concept of 'Kalala' (one without direct ascendants or descendants), explaining that in the absence of a father, certain sibling groups do not inherit because the deceased is not classified as a Kalala in this specific configuration. This hadith is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for resolving apparent contradictions in Surah An-Nisa regarding the distribution of the mother's portion when multiple sibling types are present.
